author: ojiudezue
title: Config-first rule; HVAC entry dwell 2->0 and vacancy grace 10->5 by knob; occupancy fast path parked
summary: Before planning any code, check whether a live knob, options field, HA setting or operator action fixes it (CLAUDE.md, ura-kanban gate 1b, planner/builder defs). Applied the same evening: HVAC entry dwell set to 0 and vacancy grace to 5 min as knob turns instead of building the occupancy fast path, which was parked pending real-world entry-latency measurements.
why: On 2026-09-26 three planned changes turned out to be a knob, a knob, and a non-problem refuted by data (override-expiry reclaim: 22 expiries, 0 lockouts). Dwell 0 delivers the bulk of the entry-latency gain; the fast path's margin was about half the remaining wait for a new cross-coordinator trigger path. Operator resisted dwell 0 earlier over hysteresis; the measured hold/tail structure (lighting STATE_OCCUPIED held ~300 s + per-room tails) already damps flaps.
alternatives_considered: Build the W2 occupancy fast path now (REV 4 plan) — parked
HVAC-clock entry-dwell rewrite anchored on the room clock — superseded; operator: room clock is the lighting-decay clock, HVAC needs its own
Whole-number nudge sizes to dodge echo detection — rejected; timing, not rounding, caused the false overrides
implications: Flap rate and entry latency under dwell 0 / grace 5 must be measured after occupied days (card HVAC-ENTRY-DWELL-ROOM-CLOCK-1 = Stage B arming-edge discrimination if flaps are material). Every new plan states which knob it checked first.
revisit_trigger: Measured zone flap rate materially up after dwell 0, or entry latency still > one tick on occupied days.
